symptoms.title: Headache

cats.name: Simple analgesics (e.g., paracetamol, ibuprofen)
cats.why: May relieve mild tension-type headache if suitable for the person.

symptoms.refer: Sudden "worst ever" headache, stiff neck, confusion, weakness, head injury, visual disturbance, headache in pregnancy with swelling, or new headache over 50.

symptoms.title: Fever

cats.name: Antipyretic analgesics (paracetamol, ibuprofen)
cats.why: Can reduce fever and discomfort; choose age-appropriate formulations.

symptoms.refer: Infant under 3 months with ≥38 °C, fever > 3 days, non-blanching rash, breathing difficulty, stiff neck, drowsiness, or dehydration.

symptoms.title: Sore throat

cats.name: Simple analgesics
cats.why: May ease pain and fever if suitable.

symptoms.refer: Difficulty swallowing or breathing, drooling, high fever, symptoms > 1 week, or immunocompromised.

symptoms.title: Dry cough

cats.name: Cough suppressants (e.g., dextromethorphan)
cats.why: Considered for short-term dry cough in adults.

cats.name: Soothing linctus (glycerin/honey)
cats.why: Demulcent; can soothe an irritated throat.

symptoms.refer: Cough > 3 weeks, blood in phlegm, breathlessness, chest pain, weight loss, night sweats.

symptoms.title: Chesty cough
symptoms.refer: Green/bloody sputum with fever, breathlessness, chest pain, cough > 3 weeks.

symptoms.title: Cough
symptoms.refer: Cough > 3 weeks, blood, breathlessness, chest pain, weight loss, night sweats.

symptoms.title: Nasal congestion

cats.name: Steam inhalation (menthol/eucalyptus)
cats.why: May relieve the feeling of congestion.

symptoms.refer: Symptoms > 10 days, severe facial pain, high fever. Oral decongestants: avoid in high blood pressure.

symptoms.title: Allergic rhinitis (hay fever)

cats.name: Low-sedating antihistamines (cetirizine, loratadine, fexofenadine)
cats.why: Commonly used for hay fever; less drowsiness.

symptoms.refer: Wheeze, breathlessness, or no improvement with treatment.

symptoms.title: Heartburn / indigestion

cats.name: Antacids
cats.why: Neutralise stomach acid for quick relief.

cats.name: Alginates
cats.why: Form a protective raft over stomach contents.

symptoms.refer: Chest pain spreading to arm/jaw, difficulty swallowing, weight loss, vomiting blood, black stools, age > 55 with new symptoms.

symptoms.title: Diarrhoea

cats.name: Oral rehydration salts (ORS)
cats.why: Replaces fluids and electrolytes — first priority.

cats.name: Antimotility (loperamide) — adults only
cats.why: Short-term symptom relief if no blood or fever.

symptoms.refer: Blood in stool, high fever, signs of dehydration, infants/elderly, > 48 hours, recent travel with severe symptoms.

symptoms.title: Constipation

cats.name: Bulk-forming laxatives (ispaghula)
cats.why: Increase stool bulk; take with water.

symptoms.refer: Blood in stool, weight loss, severe pain, change in bowel habit > 2 weeks, age > 50 with new symptoms.

symptoms.title: Minor cuts & grazes

cats.name: Antiseptics
cats.why: Clean the wound to reduce infection risk.

symptoms.refer: Deep or gaping wounds, uncontrolled bleeding, animal bites, numbness, signs of infection.

symptoms.title: Minor burns

cats.name: Burn dressings / hydrogels
cats.why: Cover after cooling the burn for ~20 minutes under cool running water.

symptoms.refer: Large, deep, facial, hand, genital, electrical or chemical burns; burns in young children.

symptoms.title: Sprains & muscle pain

cats.name: Topical NSAIDs
cats.why: Local pain relief if no NSAID contraindications.

symptoms.refer: Cannot bear weight, deformity, severe swelling, numbness, back pain with leg weakness or bladder problems.

symptoms.title: Fungal skin infection
symptoms.refer: Nail involvement, widespread infection, diabetes, no improvement after 2 weeks.

symptoms.title: Itching & bites

cats.name: Mild hydrocortisone
cats.why: Short-term for inflammation (not on face/infected skin).

symptoms.refer: Swelling of lips/throat or breathing difficulty (emergency), spreading redness, fever.

symptoms.title: Sunburn
symptoms.refer: Extensive blistering, fever, chills, dizziness or confusion.

symptoms.title: Mouth ulcers

cats.name: Antiseptic mouthwash / local anaesthetic gel
cats.why: Ease pain and keep area clean.

symptoms.refer: Ulcer > 3 weeks, unexplained recurrent ulcers, painless or unusual ulcers.

symptoms.title: Head lice

cats.name: Head-lice lotions (dimeticone, permethrin)
cats.why: Applied as directed, repeated after 7 days.

symptoms.refer: Infected scalp, treatment failure.

symptoms.title: Nappy rash
symptoms.refer: Severe, blistered or spreading rash, or fever.

symptoms.title: Acne
symptoms.refer: Severe, cystic or scarring acne.

symptoms.title: Dry eyes
symptoms.refer: Pain, light sensitivity, reduced vision, contact-lens wearers with red eye.

symptoms.title: Ear wax
symptoms.refer: Ear pain, discharge, dizziness, possible perforation.

symptoms.title: Travel sickness
symptoms.refer: Persistent vomiting.

symptoms.title: Dry skin
symptoms.refer: Infected (weeping/crusted) skin, widespread eczema not controlled.

symptoms.title: Stopping smoking
symptoms.refer: Recent heart attack/stroke, pregnancy — seek advice.

symptoms.title: Threadworm
symptoms.refer: Children under 2, pregnancy, persistent symptoms.

symptoms.title: Toothache
symptoms.refer: Dentist for all toothache; urgently for facial swelling, fever or difficulty swallowing.

symptoms.title: Sleep problems

cats.name: Short-term sedating antihistamines (adults)
cats.why: Not for older adults; short term only.

symptoms.refer: Persistent insomnia, low mood, sleep apnoea symptoms.

symptoms.title: Chest pain
symptoms.refer: EMERGENCY: chest pain, especially spreading to arm/jaw with sweating, nausea or breathlessness — call emergency services.

symptoms.title: Breathlessness
symptoms.refer: Breathlessness, wheeze not relieved by inhaler, or inability to complete sentences — urgent medical/emergency care.

fridge.title: Refrigerator temperature alarm
fridge.toast: Refrigerator alarm! Temperature out of range.
fridge.text: The medicine refrigerator reads {temp} °C (required range 2–8 °C). It has been out of range for about 25 minutes. It holds insulin and other cold-chain products.
options: Record the reading, quarantine the cold-chain stock pending assessment, fix the cause (door seal/setting) and follow the temperature-excursion procedure.
Ignore it — the temperature will come back down by itself.
Move all insulin and vaccines into the freezer compartment to cool them quickly.
Sell the insulin quickly at a discount before it spoils.
fridge.learn: Cold-chain medicines (e.g., insulin, vaccines) must be kept at 2–8 °C and never frozen. Excursions are documented, affected stock is quarantined and assessed (e.g., with the manufacturer) before any use, and the cause is fixed.

expired.title: Expired stock discovered
expired.objective: Handle the expired stock in storage
expired.text: During a stock check you find a carton of {product} (batch {batch}) with expiry {expiry}. It is past its expiry date.
options: Remove it from saleable stock, label it, place it in the quarantine bin and record it for proper disposal/return.
Move it to the front of the shelf so it sells first (FEFO).
Sell it at a discount — a few weeks past expiry is fine.
Put it at the back of the shelf behind newer stock.
expired.learn: Expired medicines must never be supplied. Remove, segregate (quarantine), document and dispose of them through the proper route. FEFO (First Expiry, First Out) applies to in-date stock only.

misplaced.title: Product in the wrong location
misplaced.toast: A product was found on the wrong shelf.
misplaced.objective: Check the misplaced product on the vitamins shelf
misplaced.text: A {product} pen — a refrigerated prescription medicine — has been found on the Vitamins shelf at room temperature. Nobody knows how long it has been there.
options: Remove it from sale, quarantine it as a possible cold-chain breach, record the incident and check the rest of the shelf.
Put it back in the fridge and sell it as normal.
Leave it on the vitamins shelf so customers can find it.
Give it to the next customer who asks for vitamins.
misplaced.learn: Products in the wrong location are a dispensing-error and storage risk. Cold-chain items left at room temperature must be quarantined and assessed, and Rx items must never be on open self-selection shelves.
